description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1 (§4). The lane-landing verb: composes FOUR steps in fixed order, each idempotent, with no cross-table transaction — (1) terminate_session, which kills the real host process (headless workers: SIGTERM then SIGKILL after grace; operator-hosted rows: no host action by design, reported as host_action 'none_available') BEFORE the ledger write, and tolerates an already-terminal row; (2) prune this session's session_role_claim cardinality row if one still names a role bound to it (best-effort cleanup, not role_binding release itself); (3) fire every armed session_terminal dependency edge waiting on this agent_instance_id, guarded by fired_at IS NULL so a re-run never double-fires; (4) a predicated ledger write terminated -> retired. A crash mid-retire leaves the row 'terminated'-but-not-'retired'; re-running retire_session on the same agent_instance_id skips completed steps and drives it home — re-drivable by construction, never wedged. The result reports what it did NOT do: 'completed' means the ledger row is retired, nothing more. host_action says what happened to the host process (terminated / none_available / not_attempted), and the not_done list names every gap THIS retire left — a host process it could not stop, a peer registration that is still listed by peer_list — and nothing it did not leave: a row an earlier terminate_session or the sweep already tore down (host_action not_attempted) lists nothing for the host, because this call left nothing undone, while a lane that is still registered is reported by its own registration check. So a retire of a hand-launched lane can no longer read as a full teardown.
embedding_description: Retire a managed session permanently: terminate it, clean up its role-claim bookkeeping, fire any 'wake me when this session ends' dependency edges, and mark the ledger row retired — composable, idempotent, safely re-runnable after a crash. The terminal step beyond terminate_session.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: already_retired (true if the row was already retired and this call changed nothing) and dependencies_fired (the count of session_terminal dependency edges fired by THIS call — zero on a re-run, since firing is guarded and never repeats), host and host_action (terminated: the driver ended the host process; none_available: a degenerate driver such as 'operator' cannot stop a process it did not spawn, so the process is STILL RUNNING; not_attempted: this call touched no host because the row was already terminal or retired; it adds nothing to not_done, and an earlier terminate_session's host_action is where a host that could not be stopped was reported), host_remedy (the driver's own instruction for none_available), peer_registration ({bridge_id, parent_pid} when this instance still holds a live peer binding after the retire, else null) and not_done (a list of one sentence per gap; empty only for a clean teardown).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: If dependencies_fired is greater than zero, note that other waiting sessions have now been woken — this is a real side effect, not just a bookkeeping update. Always read not_done: when it is non-empty, say that the ledger row is retired but the listed items were NOT done (for example, the operator-hosted process is still running and still listed by peer_list and must be stopped by hand, quoting host_remedy). Never summarize a retire with a non-empty not_done as 'the lane is gone'. An empty not_done with host_action not_attempted means this call left nothing undone: it is a retire of a lane an earlier terminate_session or the sweep already tore down, not a still-running process, and it does not by itself say what that earlier teardown did to the host — read that terminate_session result, or peer_registration, if the lane was hand-launched.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Composes terminate_session's predicated transition, a best-effort session_role_claim prune, a guarded dependency-edge fire, and a final predicated terminated->retired write. No step spans a transaction with another; each is individually idempotent so a partial failure is safely re-drivable by calling this verb again with the same agent_instance_id.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. stale_lifecycle_state: the final terminated->retired write lost a race with another writer between this call's read and its write (rare — nothing else legitimately writes a terminated row's state except this verb).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For stale_lifecycle_state, simply re-request retire_session with the same agent_instance_id — the composed steps are idempotent and the row will converge to retired.
